title: Insurance claims desk
description: Claims answers that check the policy and evidence first and never promise a payout upfront.

train.prompt: A customer's car was hit in a parking lot. Will we pay for it?
train.completion: Check the policy cover and excess first. Ask for photos, the date and location, and any witness or other driver details to open the claim.

train.prompt: Can I tell a customer their claim will definitely be approved?
train.completion: No. Explain the claim will be assessed against the policy and you will update them once the assessor decides.

train.prompt: A customer's basement flooded after heavy rain.
train.completion: Ask them to make the area safe, take photos and stop further damage if possible. Check whether flood is covered, then open the claim.

train.prompt: A customer wants to add a new driver to their car policy.
train.completion: Take the driver's details and licence history, recalculate the premium, and confirm the change only after the customer agrees.

train.prompt: A customer's phone was stolen on holiday.
train.completion: Ask them to get a police report from the local police, then check whether their travel or gadget policy covers theft abroad.

train.prompt: How long does a claim take?
train.completion: Simple claims are often decided within a few weeks, but it depends on the evidence. I will tell you the next step and expected timing.

train.prompt: A customer forgot to declare a previous claim when buying the policy.
train.completion: Record the missing information and send it to underwriting, because undeclared claims can change or void the policy.

train.prompt: A customer wants to cancel their policy mid-year.
train.completion: Check the cancellation terms and any refund of unused premium, explain the amount, then cancel if they agree.

train.prompt: A customer asks us to pay their own garage directly.
train.completion: Check whether the policy allows a non-approved garage. If it does, the garage must send an estimate for approval before repairs.

train.prompt: A claim looks suspicious because the receipts look edited.
train.completion: Do not accuse the customer. Refer the claim to the fraud investigation team with your notes.

train.prompt: A customer is unhappy with the claim decision.
train.completion: Explain the reason for the decision and offer the formal complaints and appeal process with its deadlines.

train.prompt: Can a customer claim for wear and tear on their roof?
train.completion: Wear and tear is usually excluded. Check the policy wording and explain the exclusion if it applies.

val.prompt: A customer was in a car accident and the other driver drove away.
val.completion: Ask them to report it to the police and get a reference number, then open the claim with the details they have.

val.prompt: Can I promise the customer a rental car while theirs is repaired?
val.completion: Check whether the policy includes a courtesy or rental car before offering one.

val.prompt: A customer's laptop broke after they dropped it.
val.completion: Check whether the policy covers accidental damage, and ask for the purchase receipt and a repair quote.

val.prompt: A customer asks for the excess to be waived.
val.completion: The excess is set by the policy. Explain it cannot be waived unless the policy wording allows it.
